intro.text: Hudson Technologies, Inc. (“Hudson” or the “Company”), incorporated under the laws of New York on January 11, 1991, is a refrigerant services company providing innovative solutions to recurring problems within the refrigeration industry. Hudson has proven, reliable programs that meet customer refrigerant needs by providing environmentally sustainable solutions from initial sale of refrigerant gas through recovery, reclamation and reuse, peak operating performance of equipment through energy efficiency and emergency air conditioning and refrigeration system repair, to final refrigerant disposal and carbon credit trading.

The 2025 SG&A expenses included $4.0 million of severance expense. The increase in SG&A also reflected increased personnel costs amongst other higher costs.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 were $40.2 million, an increase of $7.2 million from the $33.0 million reported during the comparable 2024 period. The 2025 SG&A expenses included $4.0 million of severance expense. The increase in SG&A also reflected increased personnel costs amongst other higher costs.

nonop.text: Other income for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $1.6 million, compared to $2.3 million reported during the same period in 2024. In the third quarter of 2025, the Company recognized $1.6 million in other income from the reversal of earn-out liabilities related to the 2024 acquisition of USA Refrigerants. Other income of $2.3 million for the same period in 2024 was primarily driven by $1.8 million from litigation settlement proceeds and $0.5 million from a lease opt-out associated with the Atlanta facility.

net.text: Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $16.7 million, a decrease of $7.7 million from the $24.4 million of net income reported during the comparable 2024 period, primarily due to lower average selling prices for certain refrigerants, and higher freight costs. and higher SG&A costs, as described above.

ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $3.2 million, when compared to the net cash provided by operating activities of $91.8 million for the comparable 2024 period. The variance is primarily due to increased inventory purchases, timing of accounts receivable, accounts payable and accrued expenses.

wc.text: At December 31, 2025, the Company had working capital, which represents current assets less current liabilities, of $146.2 million, a decrease of $1.5 million from the working capital of $147.7 million at December 31, 2024. The decrease in working capital is primarily attributable to the decrease in cash and increase in accounts payable due to higher inventory purchases at year end.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $7.3 million when compared to the net cash used in investing activities of $26.0 million for the comparable 2024 period, mainly due to the 2025 acquisition of Refrigerants Inc and 2024 acquisition of USA Refrigerants as previously discussed and timing of capital expenditures.

Product.text: For inventory, the Company evaluates both current and anticipated sales prices of its products to determine if a write down of inventory to net realizable value is necessary. Net realizable value represents the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion and disposal. The determination if a write-down to net realizable value is necessary is primarily affected by the market prices for the refrigerant gases we sell. Commodity prices generally are affected by a wide range of factors beyond our control, including weather, seasonality, the availability and adequacy of supply, government regulation and policies and general political and economic conditions. At any time, our inventory levels may be substantial and fluctuate, which will materially impact our estimates of net realizable value.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the United States Defense Logistics Agency (the “DLA”) accounted for greater than 10% of the Company’s revenue and over 10% of the outstanding accounts receivable at December 31, 2025 and 2024.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the DLA accounted for 15%, 15% and 18% of our revenues.
The Company also relies on trade secrets and proprietary know-how, and employs various methods to protect its technology.
Our business operations rely on the secure collection, storage, transmission, and other processing of proprietary, confidential, and sensitive data.

We rely on a multidisciplinary team, including our information security function, legal department, management, and third-party service providers, as described further below, to identify, assess, and manage cybersecurity threats and risks.

The payment of dividends, if any, in the future is within the discretion of the Board of Directors and will depend upon the Company’s earnings, its capital requirements and financial condition, borrowing covenants, and other relevant factors.
